subject.title: QMD memory indexing can recurse into symlink loops in workspace-visible temp monorepos and fail with ENAMETOOLONG

question: Should OpenClaw solve this by requiring or probing a fixed QMD version, by adding its own pre-update symlink/cycle pruning before qmd update, or by extending QMD collection exclusions?
rationale: Current main delegates traversal to QMD, latest QMD source appears safer than the originally reported scanner behavior, and changing OpenClaw compatibility for older installed QMD versions is a maintainer policy choice.

options.title: Version-Gate QMD First
options.body: Confirm the current QMD package no longer follows symlink loops, then add doctor/status/docs guidance or a minimum-version check for affected installs.

options.title: Add OpenClaw Guard
options.body: Implement pre-update path pruning or realpath-cycle protection before QMD sees workspace collections, covering older QMD versions at the cost of owning more traversal behavior in OpenClaw.

options.title: Extend Exclusion Semantics
options.body: Wire a QMD-compatible exclusion surface, but only if it prunes before scanner traversal rather than filtering paths after QMD has already expanded them.

recommendation.title: Version-Gate QMD First
recommendation.body: Confirm the current QMD package no longer follows symlink loops, then add doctor/status/docs guidance or a minimum-version check for affected installs.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned, supplied the maintainer direction in the discussion, and authored the docs correction around this exact QMD boundary.
